title: Instrumental 1: With What? (Masculine)
description: The instrumental case answers 'Кем? Чем?' (By whom? With what?). Today: masculine singular endings -ом and -ем.
descriptionRussian: Творительный падеж отвечает на вопросы 'Кем? Чем?'. Сегодня: окончания мужского рода в единственном числе -ом и -ем.
intro: This case started life meaning 'using', and you can still see that in its name: it marks the tool you did something with. What it grew into is the widest-ranging case in Russian. Over the eight lessons that follow it will also cover who you are with, what you do for a living, how you travel, and where something is sitting. Today is just the tool.
rules: The instrumental case (творительный падеж) marks the INSTRUMENT or MEANS of an action. It answers 'Кем?' (by whom?) and 'Чем?' (with what?).
Masculine consonant nouns add -ом in the instrumental: стол → столом, брат → братом, нож → ножом, телефон → телефоном.
Masculine nouns ending in -й or -ь (with stem stress) add -ем: чай → чаем, учитель → учителем.

Spelling rule (hushers ж, ш, щ, ч, ц): when the ending is UNSTRESSED after one of these letters, write -ем not -ом. Examples: муж → му́жем (stem stress), товарищ → това́рищем, пляж → пля́жем. When the ending IS stressed, the regular -ом stays: нож → ножо́м, отец → отцо́м.

The verbs пользоваться (to use) and интересоваться (to be interested in) take the instrumental directly: пользоваться компьютером, интересоваться спортом. (Both end in -ся; you don't need to know the term 'reflexive' to use them.)
Distractors look similar but mark different roles: брата (gen / acc), брату (dat), брате (prep), братом (instr). Only the instrumental form answers Чем?.
examples: Маша пишет карандашом. (Masha writes with a pencil.) карандаш → карандашом.
Антон режет хлеб ножом. (Anton cuts bread with a knife.) нож → ножом.
Лена пользуется компьютером. (Lena uses the computer.) компьютер → компьютером.
Соня интересуется чаем. (Sonya is interested in tea.) чай → чаем.
Антон работает учителем. (Anton works as a teacher.) учитель → учителем.

items.hint: What ending marks the tool used in writing?
items.explanation: The pencil is the INSTRUMENT for writing, so it goes in the instrumental. Карандаш ends in a hard consonant, so it adds -ом: карандашом.

items.promptEnglish: Anton cuts the bread with a knife.
items.hint: Чем режет Антон? Pick the form that names the tool.
items.explanation: The bread is the direct object (acc): хлеб. The knife is the means: нож + -ом → ножом. Two cases coexist in one sentence; each ending marks its own role.

items.hint: Пользоваться takes one specific case directly. Which one?
items.explanation: The verb пользоваться (to use) takes the instrumental as its complement: пользоваться чем. Компьютер is hard masculine: + -ом → компьютером. This pattern stays the same for all bare-instrumental verbs.

items.hint: Same construction as Q1.3. What ending does a hard masculine noun take?
Учитель ends in a soft -ь. Hard nouns take -ом; what do soft ones take?
items.explanation: The 'works as X' construction puts the profession into the instrumental: работать кем. Учитель ends in soft -ь, and the stress stays on the stem (учи́тель), so the ending is -ем: учителем. We will drill professions in Lesson 4; today the form is what matters.

items.hint: Чай ends in soft -й. Apply the soft-ending rule.
items.explanation: Интересоваться (to be interested in) takes the instrumental directly: интересоваться чем. Чай ends in -й (a soft consonant), so it adds -ем: чаем. The soft ending stays soft.

blanks: Соня интересуется _____. (Sonya is interested in sport.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Спорт is a hard masculine noun (ends in -т). The verb интересоваться takes the instrumental: спорт + -ом → спортом.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша часто пользуется словарь на уроке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha often uses a dictionary in class.
errorCorrection.explanation: Пользоваться governs the instrumental: пользоваться чем. Словарь is a soft masculine noun with a stressed ending, so it takes -ём: словарём. The bare словарь is the nominative, which пользоваться cannot take.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: My brother has long been interested in sports.
errorCorrection.explanation: Интересоваться governs the instrumental: интересоваться чем. Спорт is hard masculine + -ом: спортом. Спорта is the genitive, which a learner reaches for because English 'interested in' can feel partitive, but Russian uses the instrumental here.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton opens the door with the old key.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ключ is the instrument, so it takes the instrumental. After the husher ч the ending may be -ом or -ем: a STRESSED ending stays -ом, and ключ is end-stressed (ключо́м), so the form is ключом, not ключем.

minimalPairs.explanation: The pencil here is the INSTRUMENT, so it goes in the instrumental: карандашом. The nominative карандаш would only appear as a subject ('Карандаш на столе.' / 'The pencil is on the table.').

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton cuts the bread with a knife.
minimalPairs.explanation: Чем режет Антон? The knife is the means: ножом. The nominative нож would mark the subject of a different sentence ('Нож острый.' / 'The knife is sharp.'), not the tool of cutting.

reviewVocab.definition: instrumental case (marks the instrument, means, or accompaniment of an action; answers 'Кем? Чем?')
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша пишет карандашом' слово 'карандашом' стоит в творительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: by whom? with what? (the instrumental question words)
